2027-06-17.title: Thursday of the fourth week after Pentecost
readings: Rooted and built up in Christ; the record against us nailed to the cross
The house built on rock and the house without a foundation
2027-06-17.alt: Season of Pentecost, the week after the Fourth Sunday after Pentecost. The Apostles' Fast (Shleeha Nombu) is being kept; it ends with the feast of Sts Peter and Paul on 29 June.
2027-06-17.verse: As you therefore have received Christ Jesus the Lord, continue to live your lives in him, rooted and built up in him and established in the faith, just as you were taught, abounding in thanksgiving.
theo: The monsoon has come to Kerala, and with it the yearly lesson of the rivers. We have seen how quickly water rises, how a canal becomes a river and a river becomes a sea, and how some houses stand while others crack and fall. Jesus knew such floods in Galilee, and he uses them in today's Gospel: “Why do you call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and do not do what I tell you? I will show you what someone is like who comes to me, hears my words, and acts on them. That one is like a man building a house, who dug deeply and laid the foundation on rock; when a flood arose, the river burst against that house but could not shake it, because it had been well built.” The other man built “on the ground without a foundation,” and “immediately it fell, and great was the ruin of that house.” Notice that both men hear the words of Jesus. Both build. Both houses face the same flood. The difference is hidden underground: one dug deeply, the other did not bother. The difference between them is not hearing but doing. It is possible to call Jesus “Lord, Lord” every Sunday, to sing beautifully in the Qurbono, to know many hymns by heart, and still to be building on sand, because the words we hear never reach the place where we decide how to live.

St Paul uses the same picture, and adds another: “continue to live your lives in him, rooted and built up in him and established in the faith, just as you were taught, abounding in thanksgiving.” Rooted like a tree, built up like a house: the Christian life needs both depth and growth. And Paul tells the Colossians why Christ alone can be the foundation: “For in him the whole fullness of deity dwells bodily, and you have come to fullness in him.” There were teachers in Colossae offering something more, philosophies, special days, powers of the universe to be feared and placated. Paul answers: you lack nothing in Christ. Then he describes what happened in Baptism, in words our Church sings at every font: “when you were buried with him in baptism, you were also raised with him through faith in the power of God, who raised him from the dead.” And he gives one of the most moving images in all his letters. Our sins were like a written record, a bond of debt signed in our own hand, standing against us. God took that record, “erasing the record that stood against us with its legal demands. He set this aside, nailing it to the cross.” St John Chrysostom, preaching on this verse, says that Christ did not merely cancel the bond but tore it in pieces and nailed it up for all to see, as a sign that it could never be used against us again (Homilies on Colossians 6, in substance).

Here is the rock under the house. Not our good resolutions, which are often sand, but what Christ has done: the debt nailed to the cross, the powers disarmed, the new life given in Baptism. Our part is to dig deeply: to let his word go down past our feelings and habits to the place where we choose. The Apostles' Fast, which began yesterday, is a time for digging. When we fast, we feel the ground shift a little; we discover how much of our peace depended on comfort, food, our phone, other people's approval. Underneath, if we keep digging, we find the rock that does not move. In these monsoon days, when you hear the rain on the roof at night, let it remind you to ask: on what is my life built? And pray for those whose houses are threatened by water this season, and for all who have lost homes in floods. A Christian who is rooted in Christ is not spared the floods, but is not swept away by them.
outline: Ask: do I only hear the words of Jesus, or do I let them reach the decisions of my day?
Both hear, both build, both face the river; only one digs deeply.
Point 2 · Rooted and built up in Christ
In him the fullness of God dwells; nothing is lacking.
Point 3 · The record nailed to the cross
Baptism buried us with Christ; our debt is cancelled and nailed up for all to see.
“Rooted and built up in him and established in the faith.”
live: Choose one word of Jesus you know well but do not live, and put it into practice today in one concrete act.
Before sleeping tonight, thank God by name for three things he gave you today, including the rain.
2027-06-17.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, in you the whole fullness of God dwells bodily, and in you we have come to fullness. You nailed to the cross the record that stood against us and raised us with you in Baptism. Do not let us call you Lord, Lord, and fail to do what you say. Help us in these days of fasting to dig deeply and build our lives on the rock of your word, so that when the floods come we may stand firm. Protect all who are threatened by the waters of this season, and give shelter to those who have lost their homes. You live and reign with the Father and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.
altar: The cross on which our debt was nailed stands over every altar: in the Holy Qurbono the one sacrifice of Calvary is made present, and those who were buried with Christ in Baptism are fed with his risen life.

quick: Jesus: the one who hears my words and acts on them is like a man who built his house on rock.
St Paul: continue to live in Christ, rooted and built up in him; in him the whole fullness of deity dwells bodily.
God erased the record that stood against us and nailed it to the cross.
2027-06-17.action: Do one thing today that Jesus asks of you and that you have been putting off.
2027-06-17.question: Which word of Jesus do I hear often but have never really put into practice?

family.explain: Jesus told a story about two men who built houses. One dug deep and built on a rock; the other built on loose ground. When the big rain and the flood came, the house on the rock stood strong, but the other one fell down. Jesus says that listening to him and doing what he says is like building on rock. During the monsoon we see how strong water is; we need a strong foundation, and Jesus is our rock.
family.intention: We pray for families whose homes are in danger from floods and heavy rain this monsoon.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing Jesus asks us to do that our family will really do this week?”

illus: After the great floods of 2018, an engineer from Chengannur who helped to inspect damaged houses told a parish meeting what he had seen. Along one road, two houses stood side by side, built in the same year, painted the same colour. One had cracked from top to bottom; the other had only a line of mud on its walls. Nobody could see the difference from the road. The difference was underground: the first owner had saved money on the foundation, the second had insisted on digging down to hard laterite. The engineer said that he had read the parable of the two builders all his life, but he only understood it when he stood between those two houses.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the rock on which we build. Open our ears to your word and our hands to do it, and keep us firm in every flood. Amen.
share: Why do you call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and do not do what I tell you? (Luke 6:46). Where do I say yes to Jesus with my lips and no with my life?
Rooted and built up in him and established in the faith (Colossians 2:7). What helps my roots go deeper?
He set this aside, nailing it to the cross (Colossians 2:14). Is there a sin I still carry although Christ has forgiven it?
pm.resp: Lord, be the rock of our lives.
interc: For the Church, that she may always be built on the rock of Christ and of the apostolic faith.
For all who are keeping the Apostles' Fast, that their fasting may root them more deeply in Christ.
For families threatened by floods and landslides in this monsoon, and for those who have lost their homes.
For the newly baptised, that they may grow rooted and built up in Christ.
For those who hear the word of God but find it hard to live it, that grace may reach their hearts.
pm.close: Father, in your Son you have given us the fullness of life and cancelled the record of our debt. Make us doers of his word and not hearers only, rooted in him, built up in him and abounding in thanksgiving, so that no flood may sweep us away. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, the monsoon has come, and today Jesus speaks about floods. He tells of two builders. One dug deeply and laid the foundation on rock; when a flood arose, the river burst against that house but could not shake it (Luke 6:48). The other built without a foundation, and immediately it fell (Luke 6:49). Both men heard the words of Jesus. Only one acted on them.

Jesus asks a hard question: why do you call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ and do not do what I tell you? (Luke 6:46). We can come to church, sing well and know many prayers, and still be building on sand, if the word of God never reaches our daily choices. Hearing is not enough. We must dig deeply.

St Paul tells us what the rock is. Continue to live your lives in him, rooted and built up in him and established in the faith (Colossians 2:6–7). Christ is the rock. In Baptism we were buried with him and raised with him. And God took the record of our sins and set it aside, nailing it to the cross (Colossians 2:14). Our foundation is not our own strength but what Christ has done for us.

In this Apostles' Fast, let us dig deeply. Let us find one word of Jesus that we hear but do not live, and live it. And when the rain falls at night, let us remember to pray for those whose homes are in danger. A house built on Christ will stand. Amen.
kids: Children, have you seen how strong the water is in the monsoon? It can carry away mud, trees and even houses. Jesus told a story about two houses. One was built on a big rock, and when the flood came it stood strong. The other was built on soft ground, and it fell down with a crash! Jesus says: if you listen to me and do what I say, you are like the house on the rock. So when Jesus says, be kind, share, forgive, let us really do it. Then we will be strong like that house.

intro: Theme: “Rooted and built up in him and established in the faith.”
On Thursday of the fourth week after Pentecost, in the Apostles' Fast and the monsoon: the two builders, the fullness of Christ, and the record nailed to the cross.

q: Unless the Lord builds the house, those who build it labor in vain.
But be doers of the word, and not merely hearers who deceive themselves.
points.apply: Choose one word of Jesus you know but do not live, and act on it today.

points.h: Rooted and built up in Christ
sub: The fullness of God dwells in him.
q: They shall be like a tree planted by water, sending out its roots by the stream.
and that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith, as you are being rooted and grounded in love.
points.apply: During the fast, give ten minutes each day to reading the Gospel slowly, to let your roots go deeper.

points.h: The record nailed to the cross
sub: A bond of debt torn up.
q: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be like snow; though they are red like crimson, they shall become like wool.
He himself bore our sins in his body on the cross
points.apply: If a forgiven sin still weighs on you, bring it once more to the Lord in confession or prayer, and leave it at the cross.

concl: The floods come to every house; only the house on the rock stands.
Christ is the rock, and we build on him by doing what he says.
2027-06-17.resolve: Dig deeply in these days of fasting: hear the word of Jesus and act on it.
